scope.question: How diverse are accepted camera-V2 environment prompts, how do their recurring settings/surfaces/props/language compare with established October mAIstro guidance and workbook column A, and what additional homogenization is visible in available downstream usedPrompt records?
included: All 592 accepted prompt texts from 369 final camera-V2 cases.
The 10 scene examples and reusable template in the October mAIstro guidance extraction.
The 58 base scene prompts in column A of the workbook's Eval Set Prompts sheet; the Theme Styles column-A instruction is recorded separately and not counted as a scene.
A bounded snapshot of completed downstream records containing usedPrompt, with a deterministic stratified exact-text sample.
excluded: Any claim that source-message weakness alone caused repetition.
Prompt redesign, generation calls, or edits to camera-V2 artifacts.

method.environment: Exact accepted schema field; mutually exclusive.
method.subsettings_surfaces_props_style: Case-insensitive lexical indicators. Categories overlap and are not exhaustive semantic classifications. Regex definitions are preserved below.
method.similarity: All-pairs Jaccard similarity over lowercased alphanumeric word sets after listed stopword removal.
method.ngrams: Each n-gram counts at most once per prompt; distinct-source coverage is also reported.
method.downstream: All parseable completed record files with nonempty usedPrompt at snapshot time; exact raw and structured rewrite fields are read from saved local records.

october_guidance.reusable_template_exact: A [SETTING] with [FOCAL DESK/TABLE/WORKSTATIONS] featuring [TABLETOP PROPS]. [BACKGROUND ELEMENTS] create natural depth throughout the space. Lived-in and authentic, with [SIGNS OF USE / IMPERFECTIONS]. [LIGHTING] creates a warm, inviting atmosphere.

representative_exact_snippets.text: Laptop: An open modern corporate office with multiple workstations extending deep into the space. Desks, clean shelving, plants, framed artwork, and refined workplace décor create a layered, active environment. Repeating workstations and architectural details emphasize depth and an expansive floor plan, with no hardware or devices visible. Warm natural lighting creates a polished, inviting atmosphere, with minimal blue accents through select décor details.

Laptop: A lived-in home workspace with a wooden desk holding an open notebook, spiral pad, loose papers, pens, and a half-finished coffee. Soft daylight filters through large windows and relaxed curtains, with a comfortable chair, slightly overgrown houseplants, full shelving, books, and familiar residential objects throughout the room. Warm, layered, and casually imperfect rather than styled or modern. Minimal blue accents appear naturally in a few small everyday details.

Laptop: A warm small wooden café table with a notebook, pen, and coffee cup rest on the tabletop. A modern neighborhood café extends into the background with artwork, shelving, plants, seating, and large windows. Minimal blue accents appear selectively through a few small objects and décor details.

Laptop: A modern creative office with a medium wooden table featuring a notebook, pen, and design materials. Framed artwork, a side cabinet, plants, bookshelves, windows, and layered furnishings create depth throughout the workspace. Minimal blue accents appear selectively through small décor details.

workbook_column_a.theme_style_instruction_exact: Use blue deliberately in one physical scene element per image: wardrobe, wall/panel, furniture, exterior sky, or a minimal secondary prop, never a global color cast or lighting tint on skin. Blue covers roughly 35-45% of frame, concentrated in one carrier, placement varied across images. Skin stays warm, natural, dimensional against a cooler environment. Deliver medium-high to high commercial contrast, rich detailed blacks, clean bright highlights, moderate saturation with a rich blue accent, shallow-to-moderate depth of field, realistic lens compression, for a confident, punchy, premium campaign photography feel.

Leaning over a dark, well-worn wooden workbench in a sunlit jewelry studio, a woman in a navy top and blue apron types on a NOTEBOOK-Cheddar_13_NB_ANI with one hand while reaching for a small gold ring nestled in a compartmented tray with the other, hand tools, calipers, and potted plants scattered across the cluttered desk.

findings.claim: Accepted V2 environment labels are concentrated in Office: 493/592 prompts (83.28%); Education is 82/592 (13.85%) and Home is 17/592 (2.87%).
findings.scope: All final accepted V2 prompt texts.

findings.claim: Lexical scene construction repeatedly uses documents/forms/paper (416/592), writing instruments (314/592), wood/species surfaces (308/592), table/worktable/tabletop (284/592), and laminate (155/592).
findings.scope: Overlapping lexical indicators; a prompt may count in several categories.

findings.claim: The most repeated four-gram, 'a compact stack of', occurs in 205/592 prompts and all 9 sources. Multiple high-frequency phrases span all 9 sources, and same-camera/different-source mean Jaccard similarity exceeds the overall same-source mean. Repetition therefore is not isolated to one weak source.
findings.scope: All accepted V2 texts; lexical similarity does not establish causal attribution.

findings.claim: The October guidance deliberately demonstrates four named setting families and its template asks for background depth, lived-in signs, imperfections, and lighting. Workbook column A contains additional outdoor/urban, healthcare, gaming, retail/craft, kitchen, bedroom, library, studio, café, and office examples. V2 has some café and creative-studio indicators but no outdoor/urban, healthcare, or gaming indicators in accepted text.
findings.scope: Lexical indicators over 10 guidance examples, 58 workbook scenes, and 592 V2 prompts; corpora serve different product/task constraints.

findings.claim: Plants/greenery and windows appear in 0/592 accepted V2 prompts, versus 9/10 and 4/10 October examples and 11/58 and 22/58 workbook scenes. This is a measured corpus difference, not by itself a recommendation to add those elements to tight camera prompts.

In the bounded downstream snapshot, the rewrite adds a common rendering scaffold to nearly every accessible row: shallow depth of field, flush placement, and no-occlusion language occur in every usedPrompt despite being absent from every raw accepted prompt; soft cool daylight and teal-cyan grading are also frequent additions.
findings.scope: Incomplete and laptop-heavy downstream snapshot; counts and exact sample are stored in downstream_used_prompt_snapshot.

design_relevant_evidence_not_prompt_auth: Measure diversity at the bank level as well as per prompt; individually valid prompts can still form a repetitive bank.
Keep camera-density constraints stratified in evaluation because tight, medium, and wide prompts have different legitimate scene-detail ceilings.
Track environment/subsetting, surface, prop bundle, lighting phrase, and opening construction separately; changing one dimension does not establish overall diversity.
Evaluate raw writer output separately from downstream usedPrompt because the endpoint adds its own repeated composition, lighting, background, and prop language.
Treat source relevance as a constraint and a stratum, not as a claim that all diversity limitations originate in source messaging.
caveats: The lexical taxonomies are transparent indicators, not a human semantic annotation set. They can miss synonyms and count a term used in a negation.

October guidance and workbook scenes are broader creative references. Many include people, target products, secondary hardware, rich backgrounds, or explicit camera/style instructions that camera-V2 intentionally omits or restricts.
The 592-prompt denominator weights each generated prompt, so sources that yielded more prompts contribute more rows. Per-source counts are retained to expose that weighting.
Camera profiles deliberately constrain tight views; corpus-level plant/window absence and prop concentration should not be interpreted without the by-framing evidence.
Downstream generation was still active at snapshot time. The saved sample is strongly laptop-heavy and cannot establish printer rewrite prevalence.
Jaccard similarity is lexical and bag-of-words; it does not measure visual diversity or semantic equivalence.
No image pixels were reviewed in this bounded audit.
